## Administrative information

- Amendment identifier: `003`
- Applies to: protocol version 1.0 and statistical analysis plan version 1.0
- Status: reporting amendment after production of the regional estimates and
  before preparation of the final report
- Previous amendments: `001` and `002`

## Rationale

Amendment 002 prespecified regional maps where they improve interpretation.
This amendment documents the exact geographic source, join rules and display
conventions used to implement those maps reproducibly. It introduces no new
estimand, statistical comparison or causal interpretation.

## Geographic source

Regional boundaries are taken from the 2025 Etalab *Contours administratifs*
dataset at 100-metre generalisation. The dataset is derived from IGN ADMIN
EXPRESS and distributed under the French Open Licence 2.0.

The uncompressed GeoJSON snapshot is stored as
`data/geography/france_regions_2025_100m.geojson`. Its source URL, download
date, compressed and uncompressed SHA-256 checksums, coordinate reference
system and licence are recorded in
`data/metadata/geographic_sources.csv`.

## Geographic join rules

The Open Medic analytical geography contains 13 groupings rather than the 13
current metropolitan administrative regions plus five individual DROM:

- metropolitan codes are joined directly to their official geometries;
- official geometry code `94` (Corse) is assigned the same analytical value as
  code `93`, because the Open Medic grouping combines
  Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur and Corse;
- Open Medic code `5` is available only as a combined overseas grouping;
- the five DROM geometries (`01`, `02`, `03`, `04`, `06`) are therefore shown
  as unfilled contextual outlines and are not assigned individual estimates;
  and
- the combined `BEN_REG = 5` estimate is displayed separately as an aggregate
  value.

These rules prevent a combined overseas estimate from being visually
misrepresented as five territory-specific rates.

## Geometry quality control

The cartographic pipeline will:

1. verify the SHA-256 checksum of the stored geographic snapshot;
2. select exactly 13 metropolitan and five DROM geometries;
3. record geometry validity before repair;
4. repair invalid geometries using `sf::st_make_valid()`;
5. verify validity after repair;
6. require all 13 metropolitan shapes to match an analytical estimate;
7. verify that the DROM shapes remain unjoined by design; and
8. record the complete join audit in
   `output/tables/qc_08_geospatial_join.csv`.

## Planned figures

### Main figure

The main choropleth will show 2025 age-sex-standardised beneficiary rates for
the metropolitan analytical groupings. It will include a separate card for the
combined overseas estimate and contextual, unfilled outlines of the five DROM.

### Temporal supplement

A common-scale panel will show metropolitan age-sex-standardised rates for
2022–2025. It begins in 2022 because all regional groupings have complete point
estimates from that year onward. The 2020–2021 standardisation results include
disclosure-control bounds; selecting an arbitrary midpoint for a choropleth
would conceal that uncertainty.

The existing tabular and interval-based outputs remain the authoritative
presentation of the 2020–2021 standardisation results.

## Interpretation

The maps are descriptive representations of aggregate reimbursement data.
They do not identify individual-level exposure, treatment effectiveness,
clinical need or causal regional effects. Geographic differences may reflect
population structure, prescribing, access, indication mix, data construction
and other measured or unmeasured factors.

## Consequences for versioning

Figure-linked data and geographic QC outputs created under this amendment will
record:

- `amendment_id = "003"`; and
- `analysis_version = "sap-v1.0-amendments-001-002-003"`.
